dishes.name: Gâteau basque
dishes.desc: Shortcrust pastry filled with pastry cream or black cherry jam. The signature Basque Country dessert, sold in every bakery in Biarritz and Bayonne.

dishes.name: Piperade
dishes.desc: Stew of tomatoes, green peppers and onion with Espelette chilli, often topped with scrambled egg or ham. A staple of Basque home cooking.

dishes.name: Axoa
dishes.desc: Minced veal simmered with onion, peppers and Espelette chilli, served with potatoes. A Basque lunch dish found in local restaurants.

dishes.name: Bayonne ham
dishes.desc: Salt-cured ham aged at least seven months, from the Adour basin around Bayonne. Eaten thinly sliced, with piperade or in sandwiches.

dishes.name: Basque chocolate
dishes.desc: Bayonne has made chocolate since the 17th century. Dark bars, hot chocolate and chocolate-covered sweets from local chocolatiers are a regional tradition.

dishes.name: Ttoro
dishes.desc: Basque fish stew of hake, conger and shellfish with peppers and tomato. The traditional fishermen's dish of the coast around Saint-Jean-de-Luz and Biarritz.
